_note: Field guide text for this bird, both languages. Facts come from birds.md. A field with verified false is not shown as a fact: empty means not described, and the text says what the sources leave out. Norwegian wording is mine, Eirik to check. calendar rows: one letter per month from January, y yes, n no, ? not known.

range.en: North to Troms, scarce in Finnmark
range.no: Nord til Troms, fåtallig i Finnmark

food.en: Seeds, fruits, buds; insects in summer
food.no: Frø, frukt, knopper; insekter om sommeren

nest.en: Finely built in a fork, 4 to 5 eggs
nest.no: Fint bygd i en greinkløft, 4 til 5 egg

song_notes.en: The male has a strong, characteristic song and sings in dialects. The sources do not describe how the song sounds, so Pipp's version is a stand-in.
song_notes.no: Hannen har en kraftig, karakteristisk sang og synger på dialekter. Kildene beskriver ikke hvordan sangen låter, så Pipps versjon er en stedfortreder.

note.en: Mostly migrants wintering in western Europe, some along the Norwegian coast. The first reach south Norway in early March, males about a week before females. The sources do not give its singing months.
note.no: For det meste trekkfugl som overvintrer i Vest-Europa, noen langs norskekysten. De første når Sør-Norge tidlig i mars, hannene omtrent en uke før hunnene. Kildene oppgir ikke månedene med sang.

text.en: White rump. The chaffinch has a green one.
Its “ping ping” call is like the chaffinch's.
